prerequisites: Basic knowledge in physics and chemistry of materials
Familiarity with fundamental principles of matter-radiation interactions
Wave physics and electromagnetism (wave-corpuscle approach, electromagnetic spectrum, interaction of electromagnetic waves with matter)
Chemistry of materials (atomic structure, chemical bonds, periodic table, reactivity of materials, surface phenomena)
Crystallography and structure of materials (crystal lattice, symmetry, crystal defects)
Measurement techniques and instrumentation (understanding spectroscopy instrument operation, influence of experimental parameters)
Interpretation of spectra and data analysis (X-ray fluorescence, IR, Raman, XPS, mass spectrometry spectra, experimental errors, technique limitations)
Documentary research and use of academic databases
Scientific writing and communication (structured technical reports, analytical summaries, oral presentations)

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and select appropriate spectroscopic techniques (EDX, XPS, Raman, IR, X-ray Fluorescence, Mass Spectrometry) based on material properties and analysis objectives.
Interpret the obtained spectra by demonstrating a deep understanding of the underlying physical and chemical phenomena.
Write well-structured technical reports that justify methodological choices and the conclusions drawn from analyses.
Understand the fundamental principles of major spectroscopic techniques used in material characterization (EDX, XPS, Raman, IR, X-ray Fluorescence, Mass Spectrometry).
Know how matter interacts with radiation and how this affects spectrum acquisition.
Recognize the advantages, limitations, and application fields of each characterization technique.
Have basic knowledge of sample preparation and the influence of experimental conditions on results.
Select the most appropriate technique based on the type of material and the required information.
Perform spectroscopic analysis following proper experimental protocols.
Interpret obtained spectra to identify elements, chemical structures, and material defects.
Use software for spectroscopic data analysis and processing.
Write a structured technical report presenting results, their interpretation, and conclusions.
Be rigorous in experimental procedures and data analysis.
Be aware of the limitations and sources of error in different techniques.
Be curious and open to technological advancements in material characterization.
Collaborate effectively with experts from different disciplines.
Be able to conduct a complete material characterization analysis, from technique selection to result interpretation.
Be able to justify analytical choices and adapt methodologies based on experimental constraints.
Be able to communicate results effectively, both orally and in writing, to various audiences (scientists, engineers, industry professionals).

syllabus_topics: Nature of light: wave-corpuscle approach and quantum theory
Review of atomistics and the periodic table of elements
Radiation-matter interaction: absorption, emission, scattering
Fundamental principles of spectroscopy
X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (XRF): Fundamental principles and matter-radiation interaction
X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (XRF): Industrial applications and interpretation of spectra
Infrared spectroscopy (IR): IR absorption and molecular vibrations: light-matter interactions
Infrared spectroscopy (IR): Using IR to identify functional groups
Infrared spectroscopy (IR): Using IR spectra to analyse polymers and organic materials
Infrared spectroscopy (IR): Industrial applications and limits of the technique
Mass spectrometry: Basic principle: ionisation and ion separation
Mass spectrometry: Types of ionisation: ESI, MALDI, CI, EI
Mass spectrometry: Interpretation of mass spectra: molecular identification
Mass spectrometry: Applications in analytical chemistry, environment and biology
Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX/EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS): Principles of EDX: electron-matter interaction and acquisition of elementary spectra
Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX/EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS): Applications of EDX for chemical composition analysis
Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX/EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS): Principles of XPS: photoelectron emission and binding energy
Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX/EDS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS): XPS applications: analysis of surfaces and thin films
Raman spectroscopy: The Raman effect and light-matter interaction
Raman spectroscopy: Difference between Rayleigh scattering and Raman scattering
Raman spectroscopy: Use of Raman spectroscopy for chemical and structural characterisation
Raman spectroscopy: Industrial applications in the analysis of polymers and complex materials
Comparison and complementarity of techniques: Choice of technique depending on the material and the analysis objective
Comparison and complementarity of techniques: Comparison of the performance of different spectroscopic methods
Comparison and complementarity of techniques: Case studies and cross-interpretation of results
Comparison and complementarity of techniques: Combined use of techniques for in-depth analysis
teaching_methods: Discussions and debates around industrial and academic case studies
Group work for problem analysis and experimental strategy proposal
Case studies to apply characterization techniques
Exercises on spectra interpretation and analytical results
Individual or group work on technique summaries
Oral presentation of research results with visual support
Debates and exchanges on applications of characterization techniques
assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1*CC1 + 3*DS1)/4. Assessment is based on continuous monitoring of learning, combining several methods including oral presentations, quizzes/QCMs, short-answer questionnaires, technical reports, and case studies. No resit arrangements or minimum marks are explicitly stated.

J. J. Lakowicz, Principles of Fluorescence Spectroscopy, Springer, 2006.
R. F. Egerton, Physical Principles of Electron Microscopy: An Introduction to TEM, SEM, and AEM, Springer, 2016.

Applied Spectroscopy – Journal de l’American Society for Applied Spectroscopy.
Journal of Raman Spectroscopy – Publications sur les avancées en spectroscopie Raman.
X-ray Spectrometry – Revue dédiée aux techniques d’analyse par rayons X.
Analytical Chemistry – Journal couvrant toutes les techniques analytiques, y compris la spectroscopie.
Materials Characterization – Revue spécialisée dans la caractérisation des matériaux par différentes techniques.
ScienceDirect (Elsevier) : articles de recherche et revues sur les techniques spectroscopiques.
SpringerLink : ressources académiques en chimie analytique et physique des matériaux.
IEEE Xplore : articles sur les développements en instrumentation et spectroscopie appliquée.
Google Scholar : moteur de recherche pour trouver des articles scientifiques en accès libre.
HAL Archives Ouvertes : plateforme française pour les publications en libre accès.
Spectral Database for Organic Compounds (SDBS) : base de données en ligne de spectres (IR, RMN, MS).
NIST Chemistry WebBook : spectres de référence pour diverses méthodes spectroscopiques.
Open Spectroscopy Database : bibliothèque de spectres en libre accès.
ChemSpider (Royal Society of Chemistry) : moteur de recherche de structures chimiques et spectres associés.
Cours en ligne du MIT (OpenCourseWare) : Introduction to Spectroscopy.
Khan Academy : modules interactifs sur la spectroscopie et l’analyse des matériaux.
YouTube (channels spécialisés) : Materials Science and Engineering (MIT) – Vidéos pédagogiques sur les techniques de caractérisation.
YouTube (channels spécialisés) : Royal Society of Chemistry – Explications et démonstrations en spectroscopie.
